_why: Which pages the gates actually check. A gate that passes because it is not looking is worse than no gate, so the scope is written down here rather than implied. A page joins this list when it has been converted to public/css/synos.css and the partial markers, and it may never leave.
_phase: Phase 1 converted about.html. Phase 3 converted index.html. Phase 4 added the three platform pages and rebuilt product.html. Figures in /figures/ are always in render-gate scope. Phase 5 added build-your-own-ai.html and why-now.html. Phase 6 added the compare set and careers.html, and rebuilt about.html. 2026-08-22: legacy pages adopted the shared chrome and the kit tokens, so every marketing page is now in scope; legal pages are name-checked only. 2026-09-23: /use-cases rebuilt for software companies with agents in production; /use-cases/cloud-finops-agents deleted as internal-facing, and the two-doors figure with it. 2026-09-23: /compare and its five sub-pages deleted; build-status language removed sitewide. 2026-09-23 stealth pass: /product, /blog, /about and the three /platform pages deleted, with the product screenshots, five orphaned figures and twelve orphaned og images. /use-cases removed 2026-09-23.
_why_style_exempt: Legal and compliance prose: privacy, terms, subprocessors, security and trust. These adopted the kit tokens and the shared chrome on 2026-08-22 but their copy is deliberately NOT held to the marketing style rules. Rewriting a data-processing clause to remove an em dash risks changing what it means, and these pages are reviewed for accuracy rather than voice. Retired NAMES are still checked on them, as on every page.
